purpose: Source contract review connecting the complete index to installation and operating acceptance; does not replace the user's product requirements.
scope: All 20 GitHub repositories and 35 captured local family checkouts remain in the index. The contracts below explain cross-component behavior in the pinned sources; they do not assert installed runtime values.

research_basis.coverage: Selected documents and implementation sections were read across all five requested repositories, plus Laplace-Native. This is not a claim to have read every page. Lexical indexing is not evidence of architectural comprehension. Historical experiments, desired contracts, inspected implementation and live validation remain distinct.

items.topic: Compile target, runtime ISA dispatch and exact results
items.source_finding: The Wiki requires separate ISA kernels selected at runtime and cross-compiler golden-result checks. Laplace-Native already compiles AVX2, AVX-512 and VNNI translation units and dispatches using CPU/OS capabilities. Its tests skip unsupported ISA levels with exit 77 and optionally execute AVX-512 under SDE. The monorepo also has whole-engine target flags; inspecting that flag alone did not characterize the modular implementation.
items.consequence: A Broadwell build machine can produce AVX-512 code. Native execution of that path needs eligible hardware; compiler host, runtime hardware, emulated correctness and native benchmark evidence are separate. Identify which implementation is actually installed before changing delivery.
items.validation_state: Implementation inspected; no new native or emulated ISA execution or cross-compiler comparison performed in this review.

items.topic: Content identity, execution grain and network work
items.source_finding: Laplace describes client-computable canonical identities and native repeated algorithms over PostgreSQL set access. SQL/C# orchestrate. The Refactor execution-flow document likewise requires typed bulk execution without client round trips per record, but explicitly leaves implementation acceptance open. The Prototype README identifies a storage testbench, not the Engine; the Wiki records historical continuation experiments moving repeated work into a C extension.
items.consequence: Measure external requests, transferred bytes, boundary crossings and useful work for ingest and reads. A function named Batch or native code issuing scalar SPI calls does not establish the required execution grain. Prototype measurements are prior evidence, not current deployment results; content convergence does not remove occurrence/provenance traffic.
items.validation_state: Contracts and historical results inspected; present end-to-end network volume and execution grain remain to be measured.
items.external_research_limit: PostgreSQL documents pipelining for small operations that cannot be made set operations or COPY. Pipeline mode disallows COPY and cannot remove a dependency that requires a client response. This supports checking execution grain, not blindly enabling a transport feature.

items.topic: Numerical research is evidence, not a new specification
items.source_finding: Laplace-Research records numerical experiments on norm overshoot, libm last-bit differences, fixed-point alternatives and limits of norm-based repeat classification. The Wiki build contract and Native CORE-MATH linkage address deterministic results. The research notes label experiments and assumptions; their proposals do not automatically override the invention.
items.consequence: Preserve golden identity/coordinate/trajectory results across compiler and dispatch changes. Distinguish an experiment proposing a representation from the representation actually authorized and implemented. Wider ISA and an MKL setting alone do not prove deterministic output.
items.validation_state: Relevant research sections and implementation inspected; experiments were not rerun.
items.external_research_limit: Intel's archived CNR guidance imposes code-path/thread conditions; stronger strict-mode guarantees apply only to named routines and conditions. It is not proof of application-wide or arbitrary-library reproducibility.

items.topic: Knowledge selection, authority and workload identity
items.source_finding: The Wiki separates knowledge, authority and compute, distinguishes knowledge-package authority manifests from cache profiles, and requires enforcement before coupling and at later action boundaries. Architecture separates content storage from conventional operational state such as auth/billing. OpenBao AppRole supports machine/service authentication with policies and login constraints; an operator login does not establish a runtime identity.
items.consequence: Retain the existing Bao/Vaultwarden placement. Verify the application's own credential acquisition, renewal and permitted/denied access. Selecting a compatible knowledge target with cloud off is distinct from recovering application transactions. More compute does not confer additional knowledge authority.
items.validation_state: Requirements and official authentication mechanism inspected; workload enrollment, renewals and live authorization remain unverified in this review.

items.topic: Installed paths, resources and network reachability
items.source_finding: The Wiki gives example filesystem layouts, assigns installation/build/deployment mechanisms to Operations, and requires one named environment. It distinguishes service headroom from deliberate benchmark saturation. MagicDNS supplies device-name resolution; name resolution alone does not establish successful application access.
items.consequence: Resolve an operator-selected installation's paths consistently through setup, build, services and clients; do not turn example mount names into mandatory mounts. Budget concurrently active services and PostgreSQL operators together. Probe DNS, routes, TLS and authorization from each actual client context.
items.validation_state: Source contracts inspected. Cross-shell path agreement, aggregate host budgets and all end-to-end service paths are not established by this review.

items.source_finding: GitHub documents runner labels as case-insensitive. The previously alleged laplace/Laplace label mismatch was not a scheduling defect. The user's on-demand cloud role does not prohibit producing release artifacts there.
items.action_taken: Restored the uncommitted monorepo edits to .github/workflows/laplace.yml, deploy/linux/site.sh, tests/site-workflow.rb and tests/site-application-migrations.sh. Corrected CLOUD-ROLE-IN-WORKFLOW in this report. No delivery rewrite was committed or deployed.
items.validation_state: git diff --quiet confirmed all four delivery files match worktree HEAD 58cab06ee7b460949cb2164cb29b7e24df50c8a5. Other pre-existing Windows configuration edits were preserved.

contracts.precedence: An existing nonempty process value wins. Otherwise the selected machine.env supplies a value, with %NAME% expansion; otherwise Set-Default supplies the source fallback. An explicitly named missing file is silently bypassed in this snapshot.

The shell sources /etc/laplace/machine.env before fallback assignments. Assignments in that sourced file can overwrite process values. LAPLACE_NATIVE and LAPLACE_UCD are then assigned unconditionally from roots. OMP_NUM_THREADS and MKL_NUM_THREADS are unconditionally assigned the nproc result.

contracts.area: Windows monorepo paths and thread settings
contracts.precedence: env.cmd retains defined process values and supplies independent defaults. It does not invoke the Operations machine.env reader. It supplies a fixed 8 for several thread/build budgets, and 1 for CTEST_PARALLEL_LEVEL when LAPLACE_TEST_SERIAL is defined. Several SDK/tool paths are unconditional literals.

contracts.area: CMake paths and baked runtime fallbacks
contracts.precedence: laplace_path writes CACHE PATH without FORCE, so an existing cache or -D value wins over a changed environment. MCP's connection and host/port branches use CACHE STRING FORCE when the environment is nonempty, giving those settings different precedence. configure_file writes runtime fallbacks into headers.

contracts.meaning: Operations LAPLACE_PGUSER is the OS service account; LAPLACE_ROLE is its database client role. Monorepo env.cmd instead uses LAPLACE_PGUSER for the database login. Peer SSH identity, database login, application-state database, and selected knowledge connection are separate contracts. Credential names are indexed; values are withheld.

contracts.area: Native MCP service and request limits
contracts.precedence: serve arguments override nonempty runtime environment values, which override compiled defaults. The service reads /etc/laplace/machine.env but its ExecStart and User/Group are literal. Runtime atoi and uint16_t conversion do not establish a valid port range. This is the native MCP implementation, separate from the monorepo managed MCP deployment.

contracts.area: Modular ingestion and native table capacity
contracts.meaning: The batch variable is converted by shifting left 20, so its unit is MiB. Table sizing uses twice the expected node count, starts at 2^20 slots and grows at half occupancy. These are source-level policy/capacity controls; a virtual reservation is not committed resident RAM. TRUNKS tests presence, so a nonempty value of 0 still enables logging.

formulae.memory_domains: physical bytes / 4 for each of shared buffers, private backends and client; OS cache receives the remainder
formulae.ingest_connections: 1 + 2 * max(1, performance cores) + 2 fold slack + 3 observability
formulae.total_connections: ingest + serving + max(1, parallel maintenance workers) + reserved
formulae.private_share: backend domain / (max connections + parallel workers + autovacuum workers)
formulae.work_mem: half the private share; temp buffers receive the remainder

contracts.meaning: These are the managed planner's declarations, not a measured bound on a PostgreSQL query or all resident services. work_mem is allowed per operation; hash operations and parallel workers can multiply it.

formulae.WorkingSetBudgetBytes: max(8192 * apply partitions, client memory domain / working-set resident owners)

contracts.meaning: The constants mix declared exact structure widths and conservative accounting estimates. Their presence does not prove measured memory or wire traffic. Memory detection uses OS physical RAM before falling back to the GC memory view; readable host MemTotal can therefore win over a container limit.

NativeRuntimeEnv can either preserve existing values or overwrite them with topology values depending on the called method/force argument; MKL_DYNAMIC is always forced to 0. EnvFlag accepts 1/true/yes/on and 0/false/no/off, ignoring case and whitespace; unrecognized values fall back to the supplied default. Generic Linux topology considers allowed CPUs and the runtime CPU count; this must not be flattened into a claim that every CPU probe ignores quotas.

contracts.area: Backup retention and Windows resident defaults
contracts.meaning: Retention has both an age rule and a newest-file minimum. The Windows memory and WAL fallbacks are historical host assumptions stated in source, not a fresh measurement. Backup task and job paths are operating dependencies and cannot be moved merely because a repository is reorganized.

contracts.area: Workflow targets, release selection and operation controls
contracts.meaning: Operations resolves three dependency repositories at main in staging and passes their resolved SHAs to production. The triggering dispatch SHA is printed but is not used as the dependency checkout ref. Later jobs use clean:false and reuse prior state. The production input names hart-cloud; that alone does not establish a conflict with its on-demand development/proving role. Build execution, release tier, serving host and selected knowledge target require separate tracing. No queue:max is declared, so cancel-in-progress:false preserves the running job but does not preserve every pending request.

contracts.area: Conventional model experiment and execution controls
contracts.meaning: Model/experiment policy and physical execution budgets occupy separate TOML sections. The complete file also declares image/audio/video baselines; these are optional conventional-model concerns, not a GPU requirement for CPU Laplace. The loader reads the selected TOML path and checks that requested sections are tables; that alone is not range validation.

FoundryDefaults contains model-export recipe policy and mathematical choices, separate from host resource limits. Examples: FaithfulCap=128, relation rank band 0.55..0.95, BasisRank=256, DenseSvdMax=6000, attention/residual gains=0.5, HighwayBandCount=13, and TrajGap clamps layer count to 2..8. These should be indexed without silently reclassifying every constant as an operator-overridable setting.

contracts.precedence: TryReadConfig takes a nonempty environment value, then an explicitly selected deploy/secrets file. Its file reader returns the first matching key. ChessRuntimeConfiguration takes a nonempty environment value, then the first file with a nonempty value in its ordered installed-path list, using the last matching assignment within that file, and finally the deploy/secrets fallback. Explicit Stockfish source selection suppresses an inherited installed executable unless an executable override is supplied.

contracts.area: Computed configuration names and imported toolchain environments
contracts.meaning: LanguageFilter constructs per-source names: remove a trailing Decomposer suffix from the trimmed source name, uppercase, and replace hyphens with underscores. LAPLACE_{KEY}_LANGS wins over LAPLACE_INGEST_LANGS_{KEY}, then the global setting; a present empty per-source string prevents global fallback and resolves to no filter. Recipe expansion reads names supplied by recipe text, and toolchain import copies keys returned by the compiler setup process. These are open name families, so a finite literal-name list cannot enumerate future recipe inputs or toolchain output. Their source locations are recorded explicitly.

findings.status: verified source finding; remediation remains open
findings.finding: Linux machine.env assignments can replace caller values despite the environment-file comment claiming the caller wins; PowerShell uses a different precedence rule.
findings.acceptance: Run both real resolvers with conflicting caller/file/default values and verify one documented precedence, including empty and missing values.

findings.status: verified source finding; remediation remains open
findings.finding: Reconfiguring the same build tree with a changed environment can preserve cached paths, while MCP FORCE branches reverse precedence for selected values.
findings.acceptance: Resolve a clean build and an existing cache with -D, environment and defaults; report the winning source for each setting.

findings.status: verified source finding; remediation remains open
findings.finding: The native MCP unit reads machine.env but starts a literal build-tree executable as ahart.
findings.acceptance: Install under an alternate runtime prefix and service identity; start successfully with the source/build trees absent.

findings.status: verified source finding; remediation remains open
findings.finding: Native MCP accepts atoi-derived values that are later converted to uint16_t; CMake checks digits but not the full valid TCP port range.
findings.acceptance: Reject nonnumeric, negative and greater-than-65535 values before socket creation; explicitly define whether zero means an ephemeral port; preserve argument/environment/default precedence.

findings.status: prior role-conflict conclusion withdrawn; source wording verified; deployment behavior remains unverified
findings.finding: The Operations production input describes hart-cloud as production. The user designates hart-cloud as an on-demand development and proving server, including AVX-512 work, and has not prohibited building production artifacts there. Treating those statements as a categorical conflict conflated build location, release tier and runtime placement.
findings.acceptance: Trace build execution, artifact identity, release tier, serving host and knowledge target independently. Demonstrate serving against the selected compatible knowledge target with hart-cloud intentionally off. Do not remove a cloud build/release stage merely because its input is named production.

findings.status: verified source finding; remediation remains open
findings.finding: The dispatch SHA is logged while dependency checkouts resolve main, so the trigger does not pin the built dependency revision.
findings.acceptance: Dispatch an older known SHA after main advances; verify the produced release records and builds the intended complete revision set.

findings.status: verified source finding; remediation remains open
findings.finding: cancel-in-progress:false does not by itself retain multiple pending runs. The source comment promising queueing is incomplete.
findings.acceptance: Exercise three differently parameterized operations and verify the required retention/supersession behavior and target-level serialization across repositories.

findings.status: verified source finding; remediation remains open
findings.finding: Follow-up workflow jobs reuse checkout state with clean:false and do not reconstruct the full recorded dependency closure.
findings.acceptance: Run dependent jobs on a replacement eligible runner and verify that artifacts/configuration are explicitly restored or rebuilt.

findings.status: verified source finding; remediation remains open
findings.finding: Dividing memory by backend count is not a total bound when each PostgreSQL query can own several work_mem operations, hash multipliers and worker allocations.
findings.acceptance: Measure representative concurrent execution plans, service residency and all target-cluster connection pools; reconcile the aggregate with the host's effective memory limit.

findings.status: verified source finding; remediation remains open
findings.finding: MemoryTopology prefers host physical-memory probes before the GC/container view; a readable MemTotal can bypass a tighter process limit.
findings.acceptance: Run a limited-memory process/container and verify that the resolved budget uses the effective available limit and resident-service reservation.

findings.status: verified source finding; remediation remains open
findings.finding: The modular Engine parses batch and node-density environment values with atoll/strtoull without a demonstrated positive/range validation boundary.
findings.acceptance: Reject zero, negative, nonnumeric and overflowing inputs before allocations or ingestion; verify MiB units and the resulting table-size equation.

findings.status: verified source finding; remediation remains open
findings.finding: Presence-controlled flags and parsed boolean flags have different meanings for 0, false and unrecognized values.
findings.acceptance: Document each flag's type and test unset, empty, 0/1, false/true and invalid values at its actual consumer.

findings.status: verified source finding; remediation remains open
findings.finding: Managed configuration readers differ on duplicate keys: TryReadDeploySecret returns the first match, while the chess installed-file reader retains the last match. Quoting treatment also differs.
findings.acceptance: Resolve the same declared values, duplicate keys, quotes, whitespace and empty values through operator, managed runtime and service readers, and reject or consistently resolve ambiguity.
